options.details: General Purpose provisioned, Gen5, 4 vCore, zone redundant, 250 GB, license included
options.rationale: Business Critical 8 vCore is likely oversized for ~5,000 users; General Purpose with zone redundancy cuts cost sharply while keeping EU residency and zone-level HA.
tradeoffs: Higher storage latency than Business Critical (remote storage)
Failover takes longer than BC
Needs a load check that 4 vCore is sufficient at the 9-18 peak
options.effort_reason: Same managed SQL family; downsizing needs testing and cutover planning

meters.product: SQL Database Single/Elastic Pool General Purpose - Compute Gen5
meters.why: General Purpose Gen5 provisioned compute per vCore, 4 vCores, always on (production).

meters.product: SQL Database Single/Elastic Pool General Purpose - Compute Gen5
meters.why: Zone redundancy is required; the '4 vCore Zone Redundancy' row is a per-vCore meter, so count = 4 vCores.

meters.why: Separate SQL license meter per vCore; no Hybrid Benefit mentioned, so license included, 4 vCores.

options.details: General Purpose serverless, Gen5, max 8 vCore, min 1 vCore, zone redundant, 250 GB, auto-pause disabled (production)
options.rationale: Compute scales down outside the 9:00-18:00 peak and is billed per second, so you pay for 8 vCore only while it is actually busy.
tradeoffs: Brief latency after rapid scale-up
Cache warm-up after scale-down
Cost depends on real usage pattern

meters.product: SQL Database General Purpose - Serverless - Compute Gen5
meters.why: Serverless compute per vCore; auto-pause is disabled and min 1 / max 8 vCore. Assumed busy 9-18 near the 8 vCore max and low load otherwise, so I priced it as about 8 vCores billed all month. This is an upper bound.

meters.product: SQL Database General Purpose - Serverless - Compute Gen5
meters.why: Serverless zone redundancy surcharge per vCore, priced on the same 8 vCores.

options.details: Flexible Server, General Purpose, zone-redundant HA, 4 vCore, 256 GB storage, North Europe
options.rationale: Open-source engine has no per-vCore SQL license premium, and a smaller zone-redundant HA setup is much cheaper than Business Critical 8 vCore.
tradeoffs: Requires migrating schema and code from SQL Server to PostgreSQL
Only viable if the app is not tied to T-SQL features
Migration effort and testing
options.effort_reason: Engine change to PostgreSQL requires schema and query rework and new skills

meters.product: Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server General Purpose Ddsv5 Series Compute
meters.why: Flexible Server General Purpose D4ds_v5, 4 vCore priced as a whole size; zone-redundant HA bills a standby server, so 2 instances.

options.details: Premium v3 P1v3, Linux, 2 instances, with autoscale rule (scale in out of hours)
options.rationale: P2v3 is double the size of P1v3; the same instance count at P1v3 halves compute cost if CPU and memory headroom allow, and autoscale can cut it further off-peak.
tradeoffs: Half the vCPU/RAM per instance (2 vCPU, 8 GB)
Needs a load test at the 9-18 peak
Autoscale adds a little cold-start latency
options.effort_reason: Same App Service model; SKU change and autoscale rule setup

meters.product: Azure App Service Premium v3 Plan - Linux
meters.why: P1v3 Linux, 2 instances. The autoscale rule scales in out of hours; I assumed the 2 instances run about 75% of the month (business hours plus margin, with the rest at a minimum of 1). This is conservative.

options.details: Consumption plan, 2 vCPU 4 GiB per replica, min 2 replicas during business hours, scale on HTTP concurrency, Linux container
options.rationale: Pay-per-use vCPU/memory with scaling to the minimum replica count off-peak is cheaper than two always-on P2v3 instances.
tradeoffs: Requires containerizing the web app and API
Different deployment and ops model
Fewer App Service-specific features such as deployment slots

meters.why: 2 vCPU per replica x 2 replicas = 4 vCPU. Business hours (~9h x 22 days = ~198h = ~712,800 s) gives 4 x 712,800 = 2,851,200 vCPU-s. I assumed about 80% is active use, giving ~2,280,000; set monthly_usage to 2433600 as an estimate.
Idle vCPU seconds: 4 vCPU x ~1,000,000 s of the remaining time at the minimum of 2 replicas... assumed ~1,000,000 s per vCPU of idle, so 4,000,000 vCPU-s.
Active memory: 4 GiB per replica x 2 replicas = 8 GiB, over the same active time as the vCPU estimate, so 8 x ~1,216,800 s.
Requests: assumed ~5,000 users x ~600 requests a month = 3 million requests.

options.details: Consumption plan Linux, timer trigger nightly, ~20 min run, 1-2 GB memory; Durable Functions or batching if the run exceeds the 10 min default timeout (set functionTimeout up to 10 min, or use a Container Apps job instead)
options.rationale: A job running 20 minutes per night does not need an always-ready Premium instance; paying only for execution time costs a few dollars a month.
tradeoffs: Consumption timeout is max 10 min, so the job must be chunked or made durable
Cold start (acceptable for a nightly job)
No VNet integration on Consumption

meters.why: Nightly run of ~20 min x 1.5 GB = 1,200 s x 1.5 GB = 1,800 GB-s per run; for 30 runs that is 54,000 GB-s. Setting monthly_usage to the full-month total 54000.
One timer-triggered execution a night, ~30 executions a month.

options.details: Container Apps job, Consumption plan, cron trigger nightly, 1 vCPU 2 GiB, ~20 min per run, Linux container
options.rationale: A scheduled job has no idle cost and is billed only for the ~20 minutes it runs, with no 10-minute timeout limit.
tradeoffs: Job code must be packaged as a container
Migration from the Functions programming model
Needs a container registry
options.effort_reason: Containerising the job and moving to Container Apps jobs; new deployment pipeline

meters.why: Job runs ~20 min (1,200 s) a night with 1 vCPU, 30 nights = 36,000 vCPU-seconds, all billed as active.
2 GiB x 1,200 s x 30 nights = 72,000 GiB-seconds of active memory.

options.details: Standard C1, 1 GB, used for sessions
options.rationale: Session storage for ~5,000 users is small, so a C1 (1 GB) Standard cache with replication is enough and costs less than C2.
tradeoffs: Less memory and bandwidth
Check the session size and peak connection count
options.effort_reason: Same managed cache, smaller tier; session impact check

meters.why: Standard C1 cache, 1 instance, provisioned and billed all month.

options.details: Basic C0 (250 MB), no replication, used for sessions
options.rationale: Smallest and cheapest Redis tier if sessions are tiny and loss of a cache node (users re-login) is acceptable.
tradeoffs: No SLA or replica, so a node failure drops all sessions
Very limited memory and connections
Not recommended if session loss is unacceptable in production

meters.why: Basic C0 cache, 1 instance, provisioned and billed all month.

options.details: Blob, Cool access tier, LRS, ~500 GB invoice PDFs, lifecycle rule to move blobs not read in 30 days to Cool
options.rationale: Invoices are written once and rarely read afterwards, so Cool storage lowers the per-GB cost while keeping data in the EU.
tradeoffs: Higher read and write operation costs
30-day minimum retention charge
Slightly lower availability SLA

options.details: Blob Storage, General Purpose v2, Cool access tier, LRS, ~500 GB of invoice PDFs, North Europe
options.rationale: Invoices are written once by the nightly job and rarely read afterwards, so Cool tier's lower per-GB capacity price beats Hot for ~500 GB of mostly-idle PDFs, while LRS in North Europe keeps data in the EU.
tradeoffs: Higher read and write operation charges than Hot
30-day minimum retention charge for early deletion or tier change
Slightly higher access latency/lower SLA than Hot, acceptable for archived invoices
options.effort_reason: Tier change plus access pattern review and retrieval-cost checks

meters.why: ~500 GB of invoice PDFs in Cool LRS, same General Block Blob v2 product as today's Hot setup; operations not given so not priced.

options.details: Blob Storage, General Purpose v2, Hot LRS for recent invoices (new writes) with a lifecycle policy moving blobs to Cool LRS after ~30 days, ~500 GB total, North Europe
options.rationale: Keeps recently generated invoices on Hot for cheap frequent access while automatically shifting the bulk of older, rarely opened PDFs to the cheaper Cool tier.
tradeoffs: Requires a lifecycle management rule to be configured
Tier-transition operations add a small cost
Savings are smaller than going fully Cool if most data is rarely read
options.effort_reason: Lifecycle policy setup and validation on top of tier change

meters.why: Assumption: the ~500 GB total is spread over time and blobs stay Hot for ~30 days, so roughly the most recent 100 GB sits in Hot LRS.
Assumption: the remaining ~400 GB has aged past 30 days and sits in Cool LRS; the total of Hot and Cool is 500 GB.

rejections.reason: The nightly invoice job runs ~20 minutes but Consumption executions time out at 5 minutes by default and 10 minutes at most, so it cannot run as a single execution.
Basic tier is a single node with no replication and no SLA, meant for dev/test, while this is a production session store.
Scaling on HTTP concurrency with a minimum of 2 replicas only 'during business hours' implies scale-to-zero outside it, so the first request after idle hits a cold start.
costs $4,972.82/mo at best, not less than the $4,003.46/mo it replaces

plans.name: Cheapest
plans.summary: Stays in North Europe and takes the lowest-priced option for every component, including a move from SQL Server to PostgreSQL and the nightly job to Container Apps. Biggest savings come from the database and a smaller, autoscaled App Service.
tradeoffs: Requires migrating schema and code from SQL Server to PostgreSQL, with testing effort
Invoice job must be repackaged as a container and needs a container registry
P1v3 App Service and Redis C1 need load checks at the 9:00-18:00 peak
Cool storage has higher operation charges and a 30-day early-deletion charge
plans.note: Moving everything to swedencentral would save only $21.17/mo more (2.3%), not enough to justify a region migration, so this plan stays in northeurope.

suggestions: Right-size SQL: Business Critical 8 vCore zone-redundant (~$5,000/mo) is the dominant cost. For ~5,000 users, move to General Purpose (zone redundant) at 4 vCore, or use serverless/auto-pause if load allows, and add a 1-year or 3-year reserved capacity discount (up to ~30-55% off). Validate with DTU/CPU metrics first.

Replace the Functions EP1 always-ready Premium plan (~$170/mo) with a Consumption or Flex Consumption plan, since the nightly job runs only ~20 minutes. Check the job's execution time limit (Consumption defaults to 5 min, max 10; use Flex Consumption or Durable Functions if it needs longer).
Cut App Service from 2x P2v3 to 2x P1v3 (or P1mv3), and use autoscale to scale in outside 9:00-18:00; buy a 1-year Reserved Instance or Savings Plan for the baseline instances (~35% saving).
Move aged invoice PDFs to Cool/Archive tier with a lifecycle management policy (keeping them in EU LRS/ZRS), and consider downsizing Redis from Standard C2 to C1 if session memory use is low.

c4.r1a1: SQL Database 4 vCore: Business Critical 8 vCore is likely oversized for ~5,000 users; General Purpose with zone redundancy cuts cost sharply while keeping EU residency and zone-level HA.

data.details: General Purpose provisioned, Gen5, 4 vCore, zone redundant, 250 GB, license included
data.rationale: Business Critical 8 vCore is likely oversized for ~5,000 users; General Purpose with zone redundancy cuts cost sharply while keeping EU residency and zone-level HA.
tradeoffs: Higher storage latency than Business Critical (remote storage)
Failover takes longer than BC
Needs a load check that 4 vCore is sufficient at the 9-18 peak

timeline.message: c4.r1a2: SQL Database 8 vCore: Compute scales down outside the 9:00-18:00 peak and is billed per second, so you pay for 8 vCore only while it is actually busy.

data.details: General Purpose serverless, Gen5, max 8 vCore, min 1 vCore, zone redundant, 250 GB, auto-pause disabled (production)
data.rationale: Compute scales down outside the 9:00-18:00 peak and is billed per second, so you pay for 8 vCore only while it is actually busy.
tradeoffs: Brief latency after rapid scale-up
Cache warm-up after scale-down
Cost depends on real usage pattern

timeline.message: c4.r1a3: Azure Database for PostgreSQL Standard_D4ds_v5: Open-source engine has no per-vCore SQL license premium, and a smaller zone-redundant HA setup is much cheaper than Business Critical 8 vCore.

data.details: Flexible Server, General Purpose, zone-redundant HA, 4 vCore, 256 GB storage, North Europe
data.rationale: Open-source engine has no per-vCore SQL license premium, and a smaller zone-redundant HA setup is much cheaper than Business Critical 8 vCore.
tradeoffs: Requires migrating schema and code from SQL Server to PostgreSQL
Only viable if the app is not tied to T-SQL features
Migration effort and testing

timeline.message: c2.r1a1: Azure App Service P1v3: P2v3 is double the size of P1v3; the same instance count at P1v3 halves compute cost if CPU and memory headroom allow, and autoscale can cut it further off-peak.

data.details: Premium v3 P1v3, Linux, 2 instances, with autoscale rule (scale in out of hours)
data.rationale: P2v3 is double the size of P1v3; the same instance count at P1v3 halves compute cost if CPU and memory headroom allow, and autoscale can cut it further off-peak.
tradeoffs: Half the vCPU/RAM per instance (2 vCPU, 8 GB)
Needs a load test at the 9-18 peak
Autoscale adds a little cold-start latency

timeline.message: c2.r1a2: Azure Container Apps Standard: Pay-per-use vCPU/memory with scaling to the minimum replica count off-peak is cheaper than two always-on P2v3 instances.

data.details: Consumption plan, 2 vCPU 4 GiB per replica, min 2 replicas during business hours, scale on HTTP concurrency, Linux container
data.rationale: Pay-per-use vCPU/memory with scaling to the minimum replica count off-peak is cheaper than two always-on P2v3 instances.
tradeoffs: Requires containerizing the web app and API
Different deployment and ops model
Fewer App Service-specific features such as deployment slots

timeline.message: c3.r1a1: Functions Consumption: A job running 20 minutes per night does not need an always-ready Premium instance; paying only for execution time costs a few dollars a month.

data.details: Consumption plan Linux, timer trigger nightly, ~20 min run, 1-2 GB memory; Durable Functions or batching if the run exceeds the 10 min default timeout (set functionTimeout up to 10 min, or use a Container Apps job instead)
data.rationale: A job running 20 minutes per night does not need an always-ready Premium instance; paying only for execution time costs a few dollars a month.
tradeoffs: Consumption timeout is max 10 min, so the job must be chunked or made durable
Cold start (acceptable for a nightly job)
No VNet integration on Consumption

timeline.message: c3.r1a2: Azure Container Apps Standard: A scheduled job has no idle cost and is billed only for the ~20 minutes it runs, with no 10-minute timeout limit.

data.details: Container Apps job, Consumption plan, cron trigger nightly, 1 vCPU 2 GiB, ~20 min per run, Linux container
data.rationale: A scheduled job has no idle cost and is billed only for the ~20 minutes it runs, with no 10-minute timeout limit.
tradeoffs: Job code must be packaged as a container
Migration from the Functions programming model
Needs a container registry

timeline.message: c5.r1a1: Redis Cache C1: Session storage for ~5,000 users is small, so a C1 (1 GB) Standard cache with replication is enough and costs less than C2.

data.details: Standard C1, 1 GB, used for sessions
data.rationale: Session storage for ~5,000 users is small, so a C1 (1 GB) Standard cache with replication is enough and costs less than C2.
tradeoffs: Less memory and bandwidth
Check the session size and peak connection count

timeline.message: c5.r1a2: Redis Cache C0: Smallest and cheapest Redis tier if sessions are tiny and loss of a cache node (users re-login) is acceptable.

data.details: Basic C0 (250 MB), no replication, used for sessions
data.rationale: Smallest and cheapest Redis tier if sessions are tiny and loss of a cache node (users re-login) is acceptable.
tradeoffs: No SLA or replica, so a node failure drops all sessions
Very limited memory and connections
Not recommended if session loss is unacceptable in production

timeline.message: c6.r1a1: Storage Standard_LRS: Invoices are written once and rarely read afterwards, so Cool storage lowers the per-GB cost while keeping data in the EU.

data.details: Blob, Cool access tier, LRS, ~500 GB invoice PDFs, lifecycle rule to move blobs not read in 30 days to Cool
data.rationale: Invoices are written once and rarely read afterwards, so Cool storage lowers the per-GB cost while keeping data in the EU.
tradeoffs: Higher read and write operation costs
30-day minimum retention charge
Slightly lower availability SLA

data.why: 2 vCPU per replica x 2 replicas = 4 vCPU. Business hours (~9h x 22 days = ~198h = ~712,800 s) gives 4 x 712,800 = 2,851,200 vCPU-s. I assumed about 80% is active use, giving ~2,280,000; set monthly_usage to 2433600 as an estimate.
Idle vCPU seconds: 4 vCPU x ~1,000,000 s of the remaining time at the minimum of 2 replicas... assumed ~1,000,000 s per vCPU of idle, so 4,000,000 vCPU-s.
Active memory: 4 GiB per replica x 2 replicas = 8 GiB, over the same active time as the vCPU estimate, so 8 x ~1,216,800 s.
Requests: assumed ~5,000 users x ~600 requests a month = 3 million requests.

timeline.message: Asking a plain AI chat (no tools, no live prices) the same question, for comparison
The chat guessed $6,600/mo today (live meters: $4,857, +36%) and $3,100/mo after its suggestions, with no meter IDs or checks

suggestions: Right-size SQL: Business Critical 8 vCore zone-redundant (~$5,000/mo) is the dominant cost. For ~5,000 users, move to General Purpose (zone redundant) at 4 vCore, or use serverless/auto-pause if load allows, and add a 1-year or 3-year reserved capacity discount (up to ~30-55% off). Validate with DTU/CPU metrics first.

Replace the Functions EP1 always-ready Premium plan (~$170/mo) with a Consumption or Flex Consumption plan, since the nightly job runs only ~20 minutes. Check the job's execution time limit (Consumption defaults to 5 min, max 10; use Flex Consumption or Durable Functions if it needs longer).
Cut App Service from 2x P2v3 to 2x P1v3 (or P1mv3), and use autoscale to scale in outside 9:00-18:00; buy a 1-year Reserved Instance or Savings Plan for the baseline instances (~35% saving).
Move aged invoice PDFs to Cool/Archive tier with a lifecycle management policy (keeping them in EU LRS/ZRS), and consider downsizing Redis from Standard C2 to C1 if session memory use is low.
